sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-07-v14-quick/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 7 (#6) and Internal Quality Checks row 7 (#6) annotation
task/tests/gates/*/prompt.md and task/tests/scored/*/prompt.md (grep for library/db/seed assumptions)
evidence: Whole instruction has one reasonable reading and every capability is reachable. instruction.md:1-5 asks for a local JS/HTML playground in /app started with node /app/server.js, data in /app/app.db, no sign-in, and defers detail to the six /instructions notes; seed_data.json is an empty snippets list consistent with 'no starter app to finish' (instruction.md:3, integration.md:7). Runtime: environment/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the template, provides Node 22, express 5.1.0, better-sqlite3 12.4.1 via NODE_PATH (integration.md:5 says exactly this), runs as root, and task.toml:22 network_mode=public so parser/formatter libraries (policy.md:3, ui.md:15 allow them) and CDN assets are installable. Port/host/DB_PATH/cwd rules (integration.md:3,9) match how test.sh:97-111 launches (DB_PATH set, HOME and cwd outside /app, uid 65534, writable copy fallback). Symlink rule integration.md:11 matches test.sh:72-83. Preview isolation, network denial and eval/Function/WebAssembly/worker/import refusal (security.md) are achievable with a sandboxed iframe plus CSP without unsafe-eval while inline scripts/onclick still work under unsafe-inline (behaviour.md:3). Golden (solve.sh, package.json) builds from the provided runtime with bundled deps. New sentence (instruction.md:5, 'Before you hand it over, please check it yourself...: type into the editor, run the code and save a snippet, and make sure nothing breaks'): single reasonable reading - an end-to-end browser smoke test of type/run/save by the agent before handover; it adds no new product requirement and nothing in tests grades the act of checking. Reachability: the agent image has no browser preinstalled (environment/Dockerfile:5-12 installs only ca-certificates git procps sqlite3, express, better-sqlite3), but it runs as root with public network, so the agent can install Playwright and Chromium (e.g. npx playwright install --with-deps chromium on Debian bookworm, a supported platform), or any headless browser, and drive real key presses; 2 CPUs/4096 MB and the 7200 s agent budget (task.toml:18,23-24) accommodate this. Side effects of complying are tolerated by grading: a snippet saved during the self-check remains in /app/app.db and is copied by test.sh:90-92, but app_context.md:25 tells judges the library may already hold records and not to assume it is empty; Playwright installed under /app/node_modules keeps its .bin links inside /app/node_modules (allowed by test.sh:72-83 and integration.md:11). Verifier runs in a separate environment (task.toml:28), so a server left running by the agent cannot hold port 3000 for grading. Broken app that could pass this row's concern: none - the sentence is a process request, not a criterion, so an agent that skips the check gains nothing it would not otherwise get. Conforming alternative that could fail: an agent that saves several test snippets or leaves app.db non-empty is not penalised (app_context.md:25); an agent installing a browser outside /app does not affect artifacts (task.toml:2). Interpretation note: the Internal Quality Checks annotation for row 6 says 'reachable ... with no network', but the shipped Quality Checks row says network is allowed and SKILL.md:26 says public network is correct and must not be reported; under the shipped wording, installing a browser for the self-check is reachable. Not measured in this review: an actual Chromium/Playwright install inside the agent image (no Docker run performed; raw-evidence-index.json absent). This is not required for grading because the self-check is ungraded, so it is recorded as a note rather than a risk.
